reason: The weighty bills form one axis: tightening eligibility (denying child allowance to polygamous families #1-2, limiting child allowances #8, conditions for the state daycare subsidy #9, cutting the allowance for non-vaccination #36) against widening it (pregnancy-protection allowance for more women and longer periods #4, #11, #15, #18, #22, #25, #33; single-parent benefits #10, #16, #17, #38; maintenance income test #13, #24, #26, #30; stillbirth rights #6, #27). 'Stricter conditions, even if some lose assistance' captures that axis; disagreeing means wanting wider eligibility. The price is named and no group is singled out. Off: employer sick-leave for a child's illness (#3, #7, #20), free education from age 2 (#35), tax credits (#31, #39) and public-housing eligibility (#28, #40). They are not state benefit eligibility, but they point the same way as the widening bills, so they do not distort the result much.
